source.title: On Cross-Layer Alignment for Model Fusion of Heterogeneous Neural Networks
source.authors: Dang Nguyen; T. Nguyen; Khai Nguyen; Dinh Q. Phung; Hai-Bui Hung; Nhat Ho

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses activation-based layer similarity to align heterogeneous networks as part of a model-fusion method, then reports fusion and task-accuracy outcomes. It does not test whether representations converge with scale or directly measure representational interchangeability.
record.gate_note: The paper uses Linear CKA dissimilarity to choose cross-layer assignments, but does not report the resulting CKA scores as convergence outcomes or compare representational alignment across model scale or capability. The rows below record the main reported fusion and downstream-accuracy outcomes; these do not directly measure any claim version. Detailed alignment-ablation results are not included because they likewise report downstream fusion accuracy, not representational similarity.
record.test_reason: CLAFusion uses Linear CKA layer dissimilarity and OT neuron matching as tools to fuse ResNet/VGG/MLP networks of different depths. It reports only fused-model and finetuned accuracy against baselines (its own method's performance). It reports no CKA values, no alignment measurements across scale, and no mapping-loss measure of interchangeability. Fused-model accuracy before finetuning (e.g. 65.72 vs 93.31 on CIFAR10) is a weight-averaging outcome, not a representational-map loss. So it does not test V4 or V3 directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that cross-layer alignment plus layer balancing extends layer-wise fusion to networks of different depths. They report that finetuning the fused model improves accuracy on CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and Tiny-ImageNet, and that the method improves heterogeneous model transfer. They also report potential uses in compression and distillation.
record.recipe_differences: The method adds dynamic-programming cross-layer alignment and layer balancing before applying OTFusion. OTFusion is described as a layer-wise fusion method for networks with the same number of layers; this paper does not reproduce a representation-convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that fusion accuracy varies with layer mapping and balancing choices in its ablations; it also discusses using different layer representations and dissimilarities for cross-layer alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation-based cross-layer alignment (1 minus linear CKA) gives better fused-model accuracy before finetuning than naive or random layer mappings. For ResNet on CIFAR10 it gives 65.72 vs 62.43 (naive) and 64.04 (random), Table 12.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CKA-guided layer correspondence between networks of different depth gives better weight-fusion initializations than index-based correspondence.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: The reported outcomes are primarily downstream classification accuracies rather than direct measurements of representational convergence or interchangeability. Several headline tables report averages over 5 seeds without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed alignment-ablation accuracy results in Tables 10–12 and additional runs in Tables 14–19 are not extracted; they report downstream fusion or finetuning accuracy rather than direct representation-alignment measurements.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no convergence measurement.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption data.
Seeds 40-44 are used, but no shared-feature or subspace analysis. Table 9 reports only the stability of the layer mapping across seeds, not feature overlap.
No measure of map or stitching loss. Fusion accuracy mixes weight averaging with alignment quality.
Table 9 compares layer mappings under different costs (1-CKA, Wasserstein, neuron count) as a fusion design choice, not convergence measurements.
No test of partial convergence or of its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Convergent Learning (arXiv:1511.07543) only as motivation for neuron alignment. The reader's T4/uses_without_test classification is right. All rows are method-performance outcomes linked to no version. The ablations (Tables 10-12) and the cross-seed mapping stability (Table 9) are reasonably left out.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no measurement of convergence between independently trained models.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
Although some experiments use different random seeds, the study does not measure shared features or subspaces across seeds.
The paper aligns layers for weight fusion, but does not directly test whether one model's representations can be mapped to another's with little loss.
No interpretable features or circuits are identified or compared.
The paper does not compare representational-convergence measurements across similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
No test of incomplete or plateauing representational convergence, or of shared training data or objectives as its cause.

relation.reason: Representation alignment supplies components of the proposed method; the reported accuracy comparisons evaluate that method's utility.

tranche.reason: CLAFusion uses CKA-based layer matching and OT neuron alignment as tools, evaluating fusion, transfer and finetuning performance rather than testing a convergence claim.

source_check.notes: All listed rows are method-performance comparisons, not convergence evidence; their none version links and cannot_determine states fit. Appendix B specifies best-epoch checkpoint selection for finetuning.
